Spark is on a path to deploy hundreds of megawatts of modular capacity, and every megawatt of it begins as an unqualified site on a map. As we rapidly scale our footprint of high-performance compute (HPC) and GPU-based AI infrastructure, you will define the deployment strategy, set the standards, and architect the automation platform that brings new data centers and edge sites online — at a pace and scale few companies have ever attempted. This is a senior technical leadership role at the intersection of Network Engineering, Data Center Operations, and Infrastructure Strategy. You will partner with Network Architecture to shape designs for deployability, mentor a team of Staff and Senior engineers executing your vision, and represent the deployment org in cross-functional planning with Supply Chain, Data Center Ops, and Site Reliability leadership. You're not refining a runbook — you're authoring the playbook that defines how the world's most innovative AI cloud comes online. WHAT YOU'LL BE WORKING ON - Own Global Deployment Strategy: Define the multi-quarter technical roadmap for how Crusoe deploys network infrastructure across new and existing data centers, edge sites, and backbone interconnects. - Set the Standards: Author and ratify internal RFCs and technical standards for physical and logical network deployment — cabling, optics, fabric provisioning, validation, and handoff — that the broader engineering org executes against. -

jobs.title: Director of Engineering, Flex Compute
jobs.description_text: About the Role: Power, not silicon, is the binding constraint on AI infrastructure. Crusoe is vertically integrated from electrons to tokens; generation, batteries, controls, and the cloud orchestration layer which means we can credibly commit flexible load to utilities and deliver on it. No other AI cloud can. Flexible Compute is the system that makes that real: reducing data-center power draw on demand quickly, reliably, verifiably — while protecting the workloads that matter most. It gets us megawatts sooner, earns more per megawatt, and rides through grid-stress events without breaking SLAs. You'll operate at the seam between one of the industry's fastest-growing energy footprints and the software that controls it. This is a utility-facing, safety-critical control system, and a ground-up build. You’ll define the architecture, ship the first production system, and build the team from scratch. This is not a traditional recruiting role: you'll work in a fast-paced, high-growth environment where strong partnerships with leaders, sharp sourcing instincts, and sound judgment matter every day. You'll join a growing Talent team that is collaborative, mission-driven, and execution-oriented, partnering closely with leadership to shape hiring strategy, candidate experience, and how Hadrian shows up in the talent market. We are looking for Recruiters within the following domains: - Technical Recruiter: Owns hiring for software engineers, product, designers, and other technical talent - Business Recruiter: Owns hiring across GTM and G&A functions - Manufacturing Recruiter: Owns recruiting across manufacturing operations WHAT YOU'LL DO - Own full-cycle recruiting for your assigned function, from intake through offer - Partner with hiring managers and leaders to define role requirements, success profiles, and hiring priorities - Build and execute sourcing strategies to attract high-quality, diverse talent - Run efficient, high-signal, compliant interview and selection processes - Deliver an exceptional candidate experience aligned with Hadrian's culture and values - Track hiring performance and use data

jobs.title: Systems Engineer, Mechanical Design
jobs.description_text: The Role Factory automation is key to Hadrian’s operations. Our team owns the responsibility of designing and delivering elegant equipment solutions that bridge the gap between our core manufacturing processes and the rest of factory operations. We're looking for someone who thrives at the intersection of mechanical systems, real-time control, and software architecture. You'll own the design and the outcome of equipment that powers our factory automation platform—working alongside mechanical engineers, software architects, and manufacturing teams to ship robust, scalable solutions. This is an ownership role. You won't just define the system, you'll be responsible for delivering it on timeline, on cost, and accountable for system performance. You'll guide the team through technical decisions, partner with stakeholders to ensure we're building the right equipment, and carry each project from concept through performance verification. You'll make the hard tradeoffs, performance vs. reliability, simplicity vs. capability, speed vs. cost, in a fast-paced environment where requirements evolve as quickly as we do. What You’ll Do - Define equipment and area design requirements, working through both the knowns and the unknowns present at conception. - Lead a cross-functional team (mechanical, controls, software, build) through the full design process — owning requirements, chairing design reviews, and driving phase gates from concept to production acceptance. - Help build the framework

jobs.title: Systems Administrator, AV
jobs.description_text: THE ROLE As an IT Systems Administrator at our Torrance HQ, your week swings between three things: writing automation, running AV for company events, and picking up escalated service desk work. You are equally at home in a code editor, at the back of an all-hands running the show, and in a Jira ticket that no one else could crack. Our conference and event stack standardizes on Microsoft Teams in a GCC High tenant. Experience with Zoom, Google Meet, or other platforms is welcome, since you will still touch them across guest events, partner meetings, and integrations. WHAT YOU'LL DO AV - Manage our Microsoft Teams environment day to day. - Configure, set up, document, and run GCC High Teams meetings so the people on stage never have to think about it. - Run live AV, hands-on, for all-hands, large team meetings, podcasts, and other company events. - Own break-fix for our conference rooms, including Logitech, Crestron, Q-SYS, and similar room gear. - Assist in standing up new conference rooms. Spec equipment, work with vendors, and hand back a room that works. IT - Build automation with an AI chatbot such as Serval. Wire it into our real systems so it actually deflects work. - Write code in PowerShell, Bash, Python, or similar to integrate systems and cut manual work. - Own ITSM workflows and integrations. jobs.title: IT Operations Lead
jobs.description_text: THE ROLE You will be at Hadrian's HQ in Torrance, CA. Execs, engineering, design, program teams, and visiting customers all work out of our Torrance campus. As IT Lead, you own the health of the team that keeps corporate IT running for our west coast operations, with a secondary lens on our factory operations. You will lead a small team of Technicians, Analysts, and Systems Admins. Two things sit at the center of the job: technical ability and leadership. Corporate IT is your main focus. Factory IT is your secondary partnership: you back up the site IT teams, keep our tools consistent between HQ and the floor, and make sure the two sides feel like one company. WHAT YOU'LL DO - Lead the IT team day to day at HQ. Set priorities, clear blockers, and get your hands dirty so the queue keeps moving and the projects keep landing. - Build and evolve our AI chatbot workflows. Design intents, wire up integrations to Okta, Microsoft 365, Box, Jira, and our internal systems, and keep the flows tuned as the business changes. - Keep a live pulse on ticket flow across HQ and the factory. Watch volume, categories, and repeat requests, and turn what you see into automation, chatbot skills, self-service, or new runbooks. - Own executive service and white-glove support. Make sure execs, board members, and visiting VIPs get fast, quiet, and reliable help every time they are on campus or on the road. - Help the team run live AV for all-hands, podcasts, and events. Own the conference rooms, all-ha

jobs.title: Brand Designer
jobs.description_text: THE ROLE Hadrian is hiring our first dedicated Brand Designer. You will own how Hadrian looks, everywhere, and you will build that system while producing the work that carries it. Be clear-eyed about the shape of this job. In the near term it is heavily hands-on. We have campaigns in market, recruiting pushes running, out of home to produce, launches to support, and a constant need for assets. You will be designing daily. Over time, as you build templates, systems, and support around you, the balance shifts toward defining our design language and directing the people and partners who apply it. The design strategy is genuinely yours to set. It just gets built while the work ships, not before it. The subject matter is an unusual advantage. We make physical things in real factories: machines, metal, parts with tight tolerances, sparks. Very little of the design vocabulary of technology companies fits us well. Finding what does is the interesting part of this role. WHY NOW We have never had a designer. Our visual output today comes from a mix of external partners and internal improvisation, which means quality is inconsistent and nothing compounds, despite our head of marketing’s passion for graphic design. Meanwhile the volume is climbing sharply: an active brand and talent campaign, out of home production, recruiting collateral across multiple sites, and launches tied to new manufacturing capabilities. You arrive with more than enough real work to do and a blank slate on how it

jobs.title: Construction Field Engineer, MEP
jobs.description_text: THE ROLE: The MEP Construction Field Engineer will serve as the site project team’s field-level subject matter expert in mechanical, electrical, and plumbing for industrial utility systems supporting brownfield construction. This position will support the rehabilitation and modernization of existing facility infrastructure as well as installation of new systems required to support advanced manufacturing operations. The MEP Construction Field Engineer will work closely with the internal site project team, design team, general contractor, trade contractors, equipment vendors, commissioning personnel, and internal manufacturing stakeholders to ensure that the project is being executed to meet schedule deadlines and in accordance with the drawings a specifications The Field Engineer will be expected to have working knowledge of industrial infrastructure to support the Superintendent in evaluating field conditions, coordinating construction activities, tracking physical progress, and driving resolution of technical and construction issues before they affect the project schedule. WHAT YOU’LL DO Schedule & Progress Tracking - Work directly with the Superintendent to drive execution of the construction schedule. - Understand MEP milestones, equipment installation dates, utility availability dates, commissioning milestones, and critical-path activities. - Participate in weekly construction planning and coordination meetings. - Perform weekly field walks and quantify installed construc

jobs.title: Tech Lead, Operational Technology
jobs.description_text: The Role Hadrian is looking for a Tech Lead of Operational Technology to own and build the security program protecting our autonomous factories and manufacturing ecosystem. This role sits at the intersection of OT/ICS security, embedded systems, physical security, and supply chain assurance. You'll be the senior technical authority responsible for protecting Hadrian's production environments from cyber-physical attacks, insider threats, IP theft, and supply chain compromise. What You'll Do - Build and own Hadrian's end-to-end manufacturing security strategy and architecture. - Secure OT/ICS environments across factories, including network segmentation, industrial monitoring, identity/access, and asset security. - Establish security requirements across embedded systems and hardware, including secure boot, firmware signing, hardware roots of trust, and JTAG/UART lockdown. - Assess and test factory environments across OT networks, firmware, hardware, and third-party manufacturing partners. - Protect against supply chain compromise, tampering, IP theft, insider threats, and cyber-physical attacks. - Partner closely with Engineering, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Security, and external government/defense stakeholders. What We're Looking For - 10+ years across OT/ICS, embedded/product security, manufacturing, or supply chain security, including meaningful hands-on ownership. - Deep knowledge of industrial environments including PLCs, SCADA/DCS, HMIs, RTUs, and industrial protocols.

jobs.title: Software Engineer, Identity
jobs.description_text: The Role As our Senior Identity Engineer, you will own workforce and workload identity end-to-end — SSO, MFA, the joiner-mover-leaver lifecycle, privileged access, secrets, and service/machine identity — across corporate, cloud, and factory systems that handle export-controlled technical data. You will build an automation-first, least-privilege identity program that shrinks our largest attack surface while keeping engineers fast. This is a hands-on individual-contributor role on a small, high-leverage security team in Los Angeles. What You’ll Do - Design, implement, and operate our IdP stack (e.g., Okta, Entra, Google Workspace, Auth0, or Zitadel) — SSO, SCIM provisioning, and phishing-resistant MFA — and build the systems around it. - Build identity systems at scale that put OAuth 2.0 / OIDC / SAML and modern authorization models (RBAC and relationship-based access control) to work in production. - Own cloud identity end-to-end — Azure service principals, AWS IAM, and workload/service identity — and tie those identities cleanly to the underlying infrastructure. - Work cross-functionally to help other teams meet their identity needs, and automate the access lifecycle (joiner-mover-leaver) and reviews. - Partner with Detection & Response and Compliance/FSO so identity telemetry is detectable, actionable, and audit-ready. jobs.title: Growth Marketing Manager
jobs.description_text: THE ROLE Hadrian is hiring a Growth Marketing Manager to run our campaigns across every channel we can buy, measure, and improve. Paid social, search, email, web, and out of home, all of it operated by you. This is a scrappy, high-output role. We are not looking for someone to manage a large media budget through an agency and report on it quarterly. We are looking for the person who writes the ad, builds the landing page, launches the test, reads the numbers the next morning, kills what is not working, and puts more behind what is. You will be measured on whether the campaigns produce candidates and conversations, not on how much you spent or how many impressions you bought. Our primary audience is technical: software and AI engineers, plus machinists, welders, and skilled technicians. These are not audiences you reach efficiently with a generic playbook, and most of the standard growth tactics will need to be rebuilt for them. Figuring out what actually works here is the job. WHY NOW We are hiring aggressively across multiple sites and running a major brand and talent campaign, and we do not have a dedicated owner for performance and campaign execution. Media is currently being planned faster than it can be operated. You are the person who closes that gap, with real budget across digital and out of home and enough autonomy to make the channel calls yourself. jobs.title: Quality Manager, SUBSAFE
jobs.description_text: THE ROLE: The Quality Manager owns program quality end to end and leads the Quality Engineering team that supports it. You will build and lead a team of Quality Engineers across the program's process areas, own the integration of NAVSEA and SUBSAFE requirements into our AS9100D quality management system, and be the single point of accountability for whether product is built to spec, on schedule, and with the objective quality evidence to prove it. WHAT YOU'LL DO Team leadership — build, lead, and develop the Quality Engineering team supporting the project across sheet metal, welding and forming, NDT, foundry and forging, machining, and additive manufacturing. Staffing and coverage — close the open QE positions on the program, set priorities, and ensure every process area has quality coverage. Development and standards — coach QEs, set consistent standards of practice, and grow special-process competency (welding, NDT) across the team. Cross-functional partnership — represent quality with Build Engineering, Operations, and the program team, and serve as the escalation point for quality decisions on Nautilus. Program quality for Nautilus — first-article inspection (AS9102), product qualification, and quality across the build from receipt to delivery. NAVSEA and SUBSAFE integration — bring NAVSEA and SUBSAFE / Material Level I requirements into the AS9100D QMS, with the controls, documentation, and objective quality evidence they require. jobs.title: Manager, Tooling Engineering
jobs.description_text: Role Summary As Manager, Tooling Engineering, you will build and lead the team responsible for the design, development, and implementation of precision tooling systems that support efficient, high-quality, large-scale manufacturing. You will set technical direction for tooling solutions across large parts and assemblies, with a focus on performance, reliability, and scalability, while growing and developing the engineers who deliver that work. You will own both the strategic roadmap for tooling and the outcomes of your team, balancing hands-on technical leadership with the people management, prioritization, and cross-functional coordination required to stand up new production capabilities at pace. Key Responsibilities - Build, lead, and develop a team of tooling engineers, including hiring, mentorship, performance management, and career growth. - Set the technical strategy and roadmap for structural and mechanical tooling that supports large components and assemblies. - Own delivery and quality of tooling programs across the production lifecycle, from concept through design, build, validation, and continuous improvement. - Partner with engineering leadership, manufacturing, quality, automation, and program teams to align tooling priorities with production goals and new capability launches. - Manage vendor and supplier relationships to build, source, and implement tooling systems on schedule and on budget. - Establish standards, design reviews, and best practices for analysis,

jobs.title: Growth Finance Associate
jobs.description_text: THE ROLE: Growth Finance owns the economics of how Hadrian wins work. We sit at the front end of every program — pricing the pursuit, shaping the deal, and structuring the partnerships and joint ventures that get new capacity off the ground with our commercial and government customers. The Associate is the analytical center of that work. You'll build the model behind a pursuit from a blank sheet: unit economics, capacity and capex requirements, rate and margin structure, and the returns case that determines whether we bid, at what price, and on what terms. You'll pressure-test your own assumptions before anyone else gets the chance, and you'll be expected to have a view — not just a spreadsheet — on whether a program is worth pursuing. Beyond the model, you'll help structure the vehicles. That means partnership and JV economics, term sheets, waterfall and downside mechanics, and the diligence behind counterparties we're considering taking risk with. You'll write the memo that goes to leadership, and you'll defend it in the room. This is a small team with a short path to owning deals outright. The work available to you scales with what you demonstrate rather than with tenure. WHAT YOU’LL DO - Build and own financial models for Hadrian's largest capital decisions — factory builds, new capability investments across welding, casting, forging, and additive, and program-level spend. This includes scenario modeling, cash flow forecasting, and spend projections. - Own the financial e

jobs.title: IT Site Lead
jobs.description_text: THE ROLE Hadrian is building a new precision manufacturing facility as part of the Red River Army Depot in Texarkana, Texas. We're looking for an Site Lead to own the buildout, day-to-day tech operations and serve as the face of Hadrian tech for the entire site. This is a hands-on role with real ownership: you'll manage endpoints, support manufacturing technicians and engineering staff, maintain local infrastructure, serve as the point person for day-2 vendors, and help visiting employees from other sites resolve issues while they're on-site. When fully operational you’ll support manufacturing technicians in the use of Hadrian’s proprietary AI platform Opus. You’ll act as a bridge between the customer and product providing valuable feedback directly from the factory floor to help further refine and develop the platform. As a remote extension of the central tech team, you'll also contribute to overall Helpdesk operations by supporting other Hadrian employees through Jira Service Management and co-managing the company's suite of SaaS tools. You'll report to the Manager of Tech Deployment and work closely with a central team covering IT, infrastructure, cybersecurity, network, and helpdesk across all Hadrian sites. What You’ll Do Site Operations - Own all on-site IT support for facility employees and production staff - Manage device lifecycle using Hadrian's asset management and MDM tools - Manage your ticket queue in Jira Service Management and drive issues to resolution - Main

jobs.title: Quality Compliance Engineer, SUBSAFE
jobs.description_text: THE ROLE: The SUBSAFE Compliance Engineer owns Hadrian's SUBSAFE and Material Level I (L1/SS) compliance: the processes, documentation, material controls, and audit posture that let us procure, receive, build, and deliver submarine-safety material without compromise. You will be the single point of accountability for whether Hadrian's SUBSAFE work is compliant, defensible, and audit ready. WHAT YOU'LL DO Material Level I / SUBSAFE material control — procurement flow-down, receipt inspection, identification, segregation, storage, movement, and disposition of L1/SS material and its remnants, per NAVSEA 0924-062-0010 and applicable customer requirements. Objective Quality Evidence (OQE) — establish and audit the records package (chemical, mechanical, and performance test data; certifications; traceability) that proves conformance and ensure OQE is complete before material is released or delivered. Certification boundary integrity — define what falls inside the SUBSAFE boundary for each part, and ensures controls, documentation, and personnel qualifications are applied accordingly. Procedures and work instructions — author and maintain SUBSAFE / L1 procedures (material handling, cleanliness, traceability, non-conforming material, escapes), integrated with Hadrian’s AS9100D quality management system. jobs.title: Production Planner
jobs.description_text: The Role We're hiring a Production Planner to own the detailed production schedule day to day and keep the factory running on time. You'll release work orders, track them through every operation, and be the person who spots a delay before it becomes a missed program milestone. You'll work with Production leadership to set priorities and resolve conflicts on the floor, and you'll keep our schedule data accurate and trustworthy in our ERP and MES systems. This is a hands on execution role reporting to the Sr. Manager of Production Planning & Scheduling, with a dotted line to the local site General Manager you support day to day. You'll apply the scheduling methodology and standard work the function is building, and you'll be a key voice in making it better as we scale. What You'll Do: Develop and maintain the detailed production schedule across all operations, keeping it accurate and executable. Release work orders to the floor and track their progress through every operation, from start to completion. Set milestone dates on all work orders, ensuring dates drive the right priorities and reflect real commitments. Partner with Production leadership to establish priorities and resolve production conflicts, making the right sequencing calls when jobs compete for capacity. Monitor production progress and update the schedule, flagging constraints and delays early, before they affect major program milestones. jobs.title: Managing Director, Government Relations - Legislative Branch
jobs.description_text: THE ROLE This role owns Hadrian's relationship with Congress: the committees, members, and staff whose decisions shape defense policy, program funding, and the operating environment Hadrian builds in. It sits inside the Government Relations pillar alongside the Executive Branch and State & Local functions and works closely — but not interchangeably — with the Chief of Staff's office and the Strategic Engagement Partnerships pillar to keep congressional engagement, budget strategy, and outside validation moving in the same direction. This is an explicitly nonpartisan role. Hadrian's mission depends on durable relationships with policymakers across the political spectrum, and this role is accountable for building and sustaining that trust on both sides of the aisle. This role starts with one direct report and is expected to grow the Legislative Branch team over time as Hadrian's congressional footprint expands. On budget and NDAA matters specifically, this role receives dotted-line support from the Principal, Government Relations — Defense Budget & Resourcing. This role also coordinates with the Head of Government Relations, Executive Branch for Legislative Branch support as needed. This role also manages Hadrian's outside lobbying consultants, directing their work and drawing on their relationships to extend Hadrian's reach on the Hill beyond what an in-house team can cover alone. This person will lead the design and deployment of AI agents to automate accounting and finance workflows, and act as the primary liaison between accounting/finance and our internal engineering teams on home-grown tooling. While housed in accounting, this is a shared resource supporting our Finance organization on systems and automation initiatives. jobs.title: Managing Director, Government Relations - Defense Budgeting
jobs.description_text: THE ROLE This is a dual-front role built for someone with 15-20+ years inside the defense budget process. The core of the job is shaping the budget build inside the Pentagon and OMB, and engaging the process by which Congress sets the defense topline — a process driven heavily by congressional leadership, Armed Services Committee leaders, and the Budget Committees. This role also requires close fluency in how funding is actually spent once it's appropriated — apportionment, allocation, obligation, and execution. Particular depth on how the organic industrial base is managed and funded, how the National Defense Stockpile is managed, defense working capital funds, and the reprogramming process is also desired. Appropriations Committee engagement and NDAA authorization requests are owned day to day by the Head of Government Relations - Federal Legislative; this role supports that work rather than leading it. Because this role's core relationships — Pentagon and OMB budget staff, Armed Services Committee and Budget Committee leadership, and the comptroller community — cross executive and legislative branches, it reports directly to the SVP, Public Policy. jobs.title: Technical Program Manager, Infra
jobs.description_text: THE ROLE: Technical Program Managers (TPMs) exist to make cross functional and cross organizational work land. A TPM owns the outcome across teams that do not report to each other, holds the dependencies nobody else is holding, and makes progress visible without pushing reporting overhead onto the teams doing the work. TPMs are not just stenographers or status chasers, but end-to-end problem solvers from discovery -> execution. As a jack or jill of all traits, TPMs get the job done no matter the hurdles in their way. As the Infrastructure TPM, you will own the programs that span capacity, reliability, identity, builder tools, and corporate IT. Your partners are Infrastructure Engineering, IT, Security, and the factory and engineering teams that depend on them. You will join a small TPM function that is still defining how it works. From managing capacity to transforming our AI development process, you will be at the heart of platform initiatives that improve the company’s operations. WHAT YOU’LL DO - Capacity: Own the capacity process from forecasting through ordering to provisioning, across factories, offices, and engineering. - Reliability: Mature the reliability program: incident management, RCA reviews, and action item tracking across the company. - Builder tools: Drive adoption of the builder tool suite that puts AI into how Hadrian designs, writes, reviews, and ships software. - Identity and access: Own account, access, and device lifecycle as headcount and sites grow. -
